text: In Descartes's metaphysics, how is the duration of a created thing best characterized?
choices: As a mode of substance — the way any created substance persists insofar as it continues to exist
As an absolute container that flows equably without relation to anything external
As the order of succession among non-simultaneous events, with nothing over and above them
As the a priori form of inner sense supplied by the cognizing mind
explanation: Descartes treats duration as a mode by which any created substance continues to exist (Principles I.55–57); it is a real feature of substances, not a separate entity, and 'time' is merely the abstract measure by which durations are compared. Choice 1 is Newton's absolute time, choice 2 is Leibniz's relational order, and choice 3 is Kant's later doctrine of inner sense — none of which is Descartes's account of duration.
